Check a panel, spells or a lookup table in one call

Source: R/ensure_panel.R
ensure_panel.Rd

The checks that register data of a common shape nearly always needs, run together and reported in one overview: what passed, what failed with its counts, and the call that gives the rows. Each returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

ensure_panel(
  data,
  id,
  time,
  periods = NULL,
  gaps_only = TRUE,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

ensure_spells(
  data,
  id,
  start,
  end,
  no_gaps = FALSE,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

ensure_lookup(
  data,
  reference,
  by,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr or c(cvr, lbnr).

time

The period column (one column), e.g. year. Any type that sorts, such as integer years or dates.

periods

Expected periods. Defaults to the periods observed in data.

gaps_only

If TRUE (default), a unit may enter late and leave early, but must not skip a period in between. If FALSE, every unit must be observed in every period.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when a check fails and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a line naming the data and how many checks failed.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

start, end

Columns with the first and last period of each spell.

no_gaps

If TRUE, the spells must also cover each unit from its first start to its last end, see ensure_no_gaps(). Default FALSE.

reference

The lookup table, for ensure_lookup().

by

Key columns, as in ensure_matched(): a character vector, optionally named to map names in data to names in reference.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

  • ensure_panel(), one row per unit and period: the key is complete (ensure_complete()), unique (ensure_unique()) and has no gaps (ensure_balanced()).

  • ensure_spells(), a start and an end per spell: the unit is complete, the spells are valid (ensure_valid_spells()) and do not overlap (ensure_no_overlap()), and, with no_gaps = TRUE, leave no gaps (ensure_no_gaps()).

  • ensure_lookup(), a table to join on: its key is unique, so the join does not multiply rows, and every key of data is in it (ensure_matched()).

All checks run, also after one has failed, so the overview shows every problem at once. The exception is a check that assumes another: overlaps and gaps mean nothing until the spells are valid, and are shown as not checked until then.

The choices are fixed where a register nearly always needs the same: a panel may have units that enter late and leave early (gaps_only = TRUE, unlike ensure_balanced()), and a spell without an end is ongoing. For other choices, run the single checks; the overview names them.

A failure is one condition of class inshape_failure for the whole overview, and carries no rows. To get the rows of one check, wrap that check in violations(), as the overview shows.

See also

describe_panel(), describe_spells() and describe_match() to look at the same data without a rule, checkpoints.

Examples

panel <- data.frame(
  cpr  = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "c"),
  year = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2020, 2022, 2022)
)
# b lacks 2021
ensure_panel(panel, cpr, year)
#> Warning: Panel cpr by year: 1 of 3 checks failed
#> ✔ Complete: cpr, year
#> ✔ Unique on cpr, year
#> ✖ Gaps in panel: missing cpr-year combinations (1 row)
#>   Missing for 1 unit
#>   By year: 2021 (1)
#> ℹ For the rows: violations(ensure_balanced(panel, cpr, year, gaps_only = TRUE))

addresses <- data.frame(
  cpr   = c("a", "a", "b", "b"),
  start = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2021-01-01", "2020-01-01", "2020-06-01")),
  end   = as.Date(c("2020-12-31", NA,           "2020-06-30", "2021-12-31"))
)
# b has two addresses in June 2020
ensure_spells(addresses, cpr, start, end)
#> Warning: Spells per cpr: 1 of 3 checks failed
#> ✔ Complete: cpr
#> ✔ Valid spells: start to end
#> ✖ Overlapping spells per cpr (2 rows in 1 group)
#>   In 1 unit
#> ℹ For the rows: violations(ensure_no_overlap(addresses, cpr, start, end))

codes <- data.frame(kom = c("955", "956", "956"), name = c("A", "B", "B"))
persons <- data.frame(cpr = c("a", "b"), kom = c("955", "957"))
# 956 is in the code list twice, and 957 not at all
ensure_lookup(persons, codes, by = "kom")
#> Warning: Lookup on kom: 2 of 2 checks failed
#> ✖ Duplicate keys in codes: kom (2 rows in 1 group)
#>   The copies are identical in every column
#> ✖ Keys missing from the reference: kom (1 row)
#> ℹ For the rows: violations(ensure_unique(codes, kom))
#> ℹ For the rows: violations(ensure_matched(persons, codes, by = "kom"))
